variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: A world knowledge benchmark is a versioned question set, evidence contract, answer format, and scoring rule used to measure whether a system can find and return factual information. Some tests ask a model to recall a fact, some provide or retrieve documents, and some require the system to abstain when the evidence does not contain an answer.
variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Separate the question from the evidence contract”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Closed-book recall
pairs.detail: The model receives a question without supporting documents.
pairs.explanation: The model receives a question without supporting documents. A correct answer tests behavior under that prompt, but it does not prove freshness, provenance, or reliable retrieval.

pairs.label: Open-domain QA
pairs.detail: The system searches a declared corpus before answering.
pairs.explanation: The system searches a declared corpus before answering. Measure retrieval coverage and reader correctness separately so one stage cannot hide the other.

pairs.label: Passage QA
pairs.detail: The question arrives with a bounded passage.
pairs.explanation: The question arrives with a bounded passage. The task tests extraction and no-answer behavior inside that context, not broad world coverage.

variants.hint: Give each part the one job only it can do, then rule out the rest. The core invariant is match the benchmark's evidence contract to the product claim.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Closed-book recall: The model receives a question without supporting documents. Open-domain QA: The system searches a declared corpus before answering. Passage QA: The question arrives with a bounded passage.

variants.title: Give each part its job

variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Read the metrics as a failure map”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Exact match
pairs.detail: After declared normalization, the prediction must equal at least one accepted alias.
pairs.explanation: After declared normalization, the prediction must equal at least one accepted alias. It is reproducible but can reject an otherwise useful answer when the alias set or extractor is incomplete.

pairs.label: Token F1
pairs.detail: Precision and recall over normalized tokens give partial credit to overlapping spans.
pairs.explanation: Precision and recall over normalized tokens give partial credit to overlapping spans. F1 does not establish that a longer generated answer is factually consistent.

pairs.label: Retrieval recall
pairs.detail: Measure whether at least one acceptable evidence unit appears in the retrieved top-k set.
pairs.explanation: Measure whether at least one acceptable evidence unit appears in the retrieved top-k set. A reader cannot extract evidence that retrieval never supplied.

pairs.label: No-answer behavior
pairs.detail: Track correct abstentions and unsupported answers separately.
pairs.explanation: Track correct abstentions and unsupported answers separately. A system can improve aggregate accuracy by refusing too often while becoming less useful.

variants.hint: Give each part the one job only it can do, then rule out the rest. The core invariant is match the benchmark's evidence contract to the product claim.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Exact match: After declared normalization, the prediction must equal at least one accepted alias. Token F1: Precision and recall over normalized tokens give partial credit to overlapping spans. Retrieval recall: Measure whether at least one acceptable evidence unit appears in the retrieved top-k set. No-answer behavior: Track correct abstentions and unsupported answers separately.

variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Operate the benchmark as a measurement system”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Freeze product-shaped slices
pairs.detail: Sample stable facts, time-sensitive facts, ambiguous queries, answerable questions, and unsupported questions in proportions that reflect the declared claim.
pairs.explanation: Sample stable facts, time-sensitive facts, ambiguous queries, answerable questions, and unsupported questions in proportions that reflect the declared claim.

pairs.label: Run one traceable pipeline
pairs.detail: Persist retrieval and reader inputs, outputs, versions, timings, and policy decisions for every item without silently retrying failures.
pairs.explanation: Persist retrieval and reader inputs, outputs, versions, timings, and policy decisions for every item without silently retrying failures.

pairs.label: Attribute before tuning
pairs.detail: Separate corpus gaps, retrieval misses, reader errors, alias failures, unsupported answers, and justified abstentions before changing the system.
pairs.explanation: Separate corpus gaps, retrieval misses, reader errors, alias failures, unsupported answers, and justified abstentions before changing the system.

pairs.label: Gate with multiple signals
pairs.detail: Require critical-slice floors, retrieval coverage, answer quality, no-answer behavior, cost, latency, and contamination checks to pass together.
pairs.explanation: Require critical-slice floors, retrieval coverage, answer quality, no-answer behavior, cost, latency, and contamination checks to pass together.

variants.hint: Give each part the one job only it can do, then rule out the rest. The core invariant is match the benchmark's evidence contract to the product claim.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Freeze product-shaped slices: Sample stable facts, time-sensitive facts, ambiguous queries, answerable questions, and unsupported questions in proportions that reflect the declared claim. Run one traceable pipeline: Persist retrieval and reader inputs, outputs, versions, timings, and policy decisions for every item without silently retrying failures. Attribute before tuning: Separate corpus gaps, retrieval misses, reader errors, alias failures, unsupported answers, and justified abstentions before changing the system. Gate with multiple signals: Require critical-slice floors, retrieval coverage, answer quality, no-answer behavior, cost, latency, and contamination checks to pass together.
